==== system
Your input fields are:
1. `question` (string)
2. `facts` (array of object)
Your output fields are:
1. `answer` (string)
2. `sources` (array of string)
3. `confident` (boolean)
All interactions will be structured in the following way, with the appropriate values filled in.

<question>
{question}
</question>

<facts>
{facts}
</facts>

<answer>
{answer}
</answer>

<sources>
{sources}        # note: write object keys as nested elements and array entries as <item> elements, following the JSON schema: {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
</sources>

<confident>
{confident}        # note: the value you produce must adhere to the JSON schema: {"type":"boolean"}
</confident>
In adhering to this structure, your objective is: 
        Answer from the facts.

==== user
<question>
Capital?
</question>

<facts>
<item>
<score>
null
</score>
<source>
p2
</source>
<text>
Paris is the capital.
</text>
</item>
</facts>

==== assistant
<answer>
Paris
</answer>

<sources>
<item>
p2
</item>
</sources>

<confident>
true
</confident>

==== user
<question>
Where?
</question>

<facts>
<item>
<score>
0.5
</score>
<source>
p1
</source>
<text>
It is in Paris.
</text>
</item>
</facts>

Respond with the corresponding output fields wrapped in XML tags, starting with `<answer>`, then `<sources>`, then `<confident>`.
